messages.subject: Epistasis n=?
parts:
Dear Karl,
 
I have used a backcross (n=142 mice) to test for epistasis. Initially I performed a 2D scan to select QTL pairs that passed the full model threshold (2D).  I then created QTL objects and using dropwise (ANOVA) to indentify QTL pairs.  We identified several interactions this way and looked at the effectplots of each QTL-pair.
 
I would like to know what would be a large enough sample size to detect epistasis QTLs with sufficient power and discriminate between signal and noise.
 
My initital feeling is that, the threshold values from a 2D scan filters out most background/noise.  Then dropwise testing using ANOVA in a QTL-object further discriminates QTL pairs based on F-statistic and so eliminates further.
 
Are the above steps sufficient or would I need to perform additional steps to contol for type I errors?
 
Look forward to your reply.
 
Thanks and Regards,
 
Eiram

messages.author: 963b6d84a823404f
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Epistasis n=?
parts: I would like to know what would be a large enough sample size to detect epistasis QTLs with sufficient power and discriminate between signal and noise.
It depends on the strength of the underlying effects.
Are the above steps sufficient or would I need to perform additional steps to contol for type I errors?

I prefer to formulate the problem as variable/model selection rather than hypothesis testing, and my basic recommended approach is that in stepwiseqtl(), as described in Manichaikul et al. (2009) A model selection approach for the identification of quantitative trait loci in experimental crosses, allowing epistasis.Genetics 181:1077-1086

karl
